steps.title: Collect ear tissue sample
steps.instruction: Place a small piece of ear tissue into a clean Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Lyse tissue in NaOH
steps.instruction: Add 90 µL of 50 mM NaOH to the tube, ensuring the tissue remains immersed; if not fully immersed, spin briefly in a tabletop centrifuge.

steps.title: Store lysate (optional)
steps.instruction: Store the lysate at 4 °C for short‑term or at –20 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Transfer and vortex lysate
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the lysate to a new clean Eppendorf tube without carrying over hair or tissue, vortex thoroughly, and spin down so that any remaining tissue is at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Neutralize extract with Tris‑HCl
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8) to the lysate to neutralize the NaOH.

steps.title: Heat incubation of lysate
steps.instruction: Incubate the neutralized mixture for 10 minutes at 100 °C.

steps.title: Prepare primers and PCR setup under UV
steps.instruction: Work under a UV light cabinet and prepare a 10 µM working dilution of each PCR primer.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix with controls
steps.instruction: Prepare a master mix for all samples containing the required PCR components; include a positive and a negative control for each gene and add extra volume to compensate for pipetting variation.

steps.title: Aliquot master mix and add gDNA
steps.instruction: To each PCR tube, add 23 µL of the master mix and 2 µL of genomic DNA (≈100 ng, ±100 ng) from each sample; keep the tubes on ice.

steps.title: Run PCR thermal cycling
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in the thermal cycler and run the appropriate PCR program (program details not specified in the source).

steps.title: Prepare 1.5% agarose gel with dye
steps.instruction: Make a 1.5 % agarose gel in TBE buffer and add Midori Green nucleic‑acid stain at a 1:10,000 dilution.

steps.title: Electrophorese samples on gel
steps.instruction: Load the PCR products onto the gel and run for 1 hour at 120 V.
